targets.summary: Use c10::contiguous_strides(size) to compute the strides (e.g. for the ROCm case) rather than returning an empty stride vector or hand-rolling the stride math.
targets.evidence: The comment sits on the output-shape logic (`if (a_is_2d) {`, line 56). It asks for strides to be computed with `c10::contiguous_strides`. In the reviewed version, the strides further down were worked out by hand: `out_stride = {size_padded, 1};` / `out_stride = {out_size[1] * size_padded, size_padded, 1};`. The merged code removes that and uses the helper instead: `auto padded_size = out_size; padded_size[last_dim] = ...; const auto strides = c10::contiguous_strides(padded_size); out_stride.assign(strides.begin(), strides.end());`. It also adds `#include <c10/util/strides.h>`. It passes the padded shape instead of the raw size, which keeps the 16-byte TMA alignment, so it does the same job. One gap: under `USE_ROCM`, `out_stride` is still left empty. The core request, replacing the hand-written stride math with `c10::contiguous_strides`, was adopted.

targets.summary: Check that contraction_dim has exactly 2 elements before reading contraction_dim[0] and [1], so a short list can't cause an out-of-bounds access.
targets.evidence: Before the change, the code inside `if (!contraction_dim.empty()) {` went straight to `const int dim_a = contraction_dim[0], dim_b = contraction_dim[1];` without checking the size first. The merged code adds a check before those reads: `TORCH_CHECK_VALUE(contraction_dim.size() == 2, "contraction_dim must have exactly 2 elements");`. This matches the maintainer's suggestion exactly, including the error message.
